raw:
The knife turns once above your plate and settles cleanly back into your hand.

Ashara watches the motion without looking impressed. “Put it down. A knife is for eating, and a practice blade is for learning where it belongs.”

Rashid nods. “You can learn without having trained before. You do not, however, become a useful substitute for a ranked fighter because you can spin cutlery.”

“Cruel,” Thessaly says mildly. “Accurate, but cruel.”

“It isn’t cruel,” Ashara says. “It’s practical. I have a bout tomorrow. If he wants to train, he can start with footwork and stop volunteering to be struck.”

Caelindra cuts another piece of roast. “A startlingly sensible proposal, considering its source.”

Ashara gives her a flat look. “No, Garvey. Not tonight. Watch the bout tomorrow if you’re curious, then decide whether you actually want lessons.”
